svg.title: Who commands whom: the king's own host, the great lords' commands, and the army they make
svg.text: General is the highest rank. There is no Marshal. Every armed man belongs to one command, and every command to one person.
summons his great lords; commands in person,
or names one General for the campaign
his own army, under officers he names
a count who holds of the king, with no duke over him
the oath, and each lord's answer
Each lord answers for his own reasons: comes in full · comes with part ·
comes late · sends a deputy · sends coin · refuses
commissioned by the king, made by merit
one to each host; the first is the senior General
enlisted: lances, bows, spears, scouts, engineers
volunteers who drill, and march when mustered
serve the crown; led by their Grand Masters
The road a soldier of no birth climbs.
The Duke: a General by right
about 30,000 at full call: two or three hosts
his counts, his kin, a trusted captain: one a host
A marquis on the border: a host
about 8,000; may fight for the march unsummoned
His counts: wings or small hosts
about 4,000 each, under a commander or a General
5 to 60 men, in a baron's company
Each man swears to his own lord, not to the king.
about 4,000: a small host, or two wings
named by him, sworn to him
EVERY COMMAND IS THREE KINDS OF MEN
Conscripts are raised by each lord in his own lands
and march in his contingent, under his captains.
A host is 3,000 to 12,000 men under one General, so a large army has several. A lord's contingent is kept whole, under his own captains.
General Aldous Marr, commanding the campaign
by the king's written word, for this campaign only
The Duke of Harrow's first host
the Duke, a General by right
his own men, under his own officers
General Sir Odo Harrow, the Duke's brother
If the king is there, he commands. If he names nobody, the Generals hold a council of war: each leads his own host, and a joint order takes a day longer.
WHERE DISPUTES ARISE, EACH FROM A GRIEVANCE ON RECORD

text.tspan: A lord stays home for his own reasons; the king punishes as far as he dares.
Two lords of one realm fight over a fief, a toll or a killing.
Who has the van; a duke who will not serve under a General of no birth.
A march lord's raid that his king must disown, back, or leave as a border war.
